subject: Long-term wallet drawdown cadence and tranche schedule
messages:
From: Daniel Park <dpark@vertexhealth.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-15T14:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Exploring committed spend options for inference usage

Tessa —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're excited about the latency and cost profile for user-facing search enrichment, but procurement needs to nail down how a multi-year committed structure would actually flow. A few asks from our side:

- We expect a ramp from ~$60k/mo in Q1 to ~$220k/mo by end of year 2 as we onboard more products.
- Procurement prefers a prepay wallet approach with monthly drawdowns and a visible burn schedule.
- They want clarity on: tranche refunds (if any), monthly true-ups, and what happens when usage exceeds committed drawdown in a month.

Could you sketch a model (tranche sizes, discount tiers, replenishment cadence) that aligns to our ramp? I can share forecast spreadsheet — attaching a clean usage export.

Attachment: Vertex_usage_forecast_2026Q4-Q4(2).csv (csv)

—Daniel
Daniel Park
Head of Platform, Vertex Health
From: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
To: Daniel Park <dpark@vertexhealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-17T10:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Exploring committed spend options for inference usage

Daniel —

Really appreciate the clear ramp numbers. I ran this by our pricing and finance teams and sketched an initial structure that balances Vertex's desire for a predictable wallet with our need to preserve unit economics as usage scales. Key points below; I attached a worked example.

Highlights:
- Multi-year commit with an annual prepay wallet and monthly drawdown cadence.
- Year 1: conservative discount (12%) on committed wallet, Year 2 onward: step-up discount to 18% if committed renewal is signed.
- Tranche approach: annual wallet split into 12 monthly tranches with an option to true-up at quarter boundaries. Unused balance rolls into the next month within the contract year (no refunds mid-year).
- Monthly overages billed at on-demand rate + 25% premium; if sustained >20% over committed for 2 consecutive months, automatic review and optional temporary burst credits.

Attachments: Vertex_V1_commit_model.xlsx (spreadsheet)

If that looks like a starting point, I propose a short call next week to agree tranche sizes and any special procurement language.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Enterprise Sales Director
Redwood Inference
From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-18T09:14:00Z
Subject: FW: Exploring committed spend options for inference usage

Quick internal notes before the call with Vertex: 

- Marcus: can you confirm the net present value impact of the step-up (12% -> 18%) if they commit to a 3-year renewal cadence? Need sensitivity for 24/36 month.
- Tessa: procurement might push for partial refunds if they underspend by >30% YOY — we should be prepared with a carve-out (e.g., roll-forward + limited refund on >50% shortfall only).
- Also add a clause that allows us to convert unused wallet to token credits that expire at contract renewal — simpler for bookkeeping.

Thanks — Laura
From: marcus_lin@redwood.com
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-19T12:33:00Z
Subject: Re: FW: Exploring committed spend options for inference usage

Summary of finance view: 

- NPV delta: moving from 12% to 18% on a 3-year annual prepay increases NPV by ~6.5% (assumes discount rate 8%, usage ramp per Daniel's forecast). I'll export a sensitivity table.
- Risk tolerance: acceptable as long as we keep the monthly overage premium and the >20% sustained overage review. That protects unit economics.
- Refund policy: recommend no cash refunds under 50% underspend; instead offer credit extension with a small admin fee for early refund requests.

I'll attach a sensitivity sheet for the call.

Attachment: finance_sensitivity_vh_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)

—Marcus
Finance Lead, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
From: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
To: Daniel Park <dpark@vertexhealth.com>, Vertex Health Procurement <procurement@vertexhealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-24T16:07:00Z
Subject: Proposal: annual wallet with monthly drawdown + tranche true-up cadence

Daniel / Procurement team —

Per our internal alignment, attached is a concise proposal and a sample amortization of the wallet across the first 24 months. Executive summary:

1) Structure: annual prepay wallet paid upfront each contract year; wallet split into 12 monthly tranches.
2) Discounts: Year 1 committed discount 12%; Year 2 (upon renewal) steps to 18% if signed within 60 days of renewal window.
3) True-ups: Quarterly true-up windows (month 3, 6, 9) — you can move unused balance forward. Refunds only allowed at renewal and only for >50% annual shortfall (refunds paid as credit or with a 2% admin deduction).
4) Overages: billed monthly at on-demand +25%; sustained >20% overage for two months triggers a review and optional short-term burst add-on pricing.
5) Reporting: daily burn dashboard + monthly slice export.

Proposal attachments: Vertex_V1_commit_model.xlsx, SOW_VH-v1.pdf

Next steps: if this aligns, we can issue a formal SOW and contract redline. Happy to take your changes.

—Tessa
Enterprise Sales Director
Redwood Inference
From: Daniel Park <dpark@vertexhealth.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Cc: Vertex Health Procurement <procurement@vertexhealth.com>
Date: 2026-10-02T09:18:00Z
Subject: Re: Proposal: annual wallet with monthly drawdown + tranche true-up cadence

Tessa —

Thanks for the clear proposal and the worked numbers. Procurement is comfortable with the annual wallet / monthly tranche model. Two small asks before we finalize: 

1) Can you relax the refund threshold to >40% for Year 1 only (we have more macro uncertainty during onboarding)?
2) Can the quarterly true-up include a one-time ability to reallocate up to 15% of the annual wallet between product lines (for example, move credit from search to summarization) without penalty?

If you can accept those two tweaks, we can proceed to SOW redlines and legal review on our side.

Attachment: none

—Daniel
Head of Platform, Vertex Health
